claims.head: Best against best
claims.body: The Stars are one of the league’s best for the power play, and the Avalanche are one of the league’s best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Stars’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots.
claims.call: The Stars’ power play creates more than the league-average 7.5 expected goals per 60 against the Avalanche.
claims.nums: Dallas 3rd for the power play (9.0 expected goals per 60) · Colorado 2nd for the penalty kill
claims.gist: It’s strength against strength: the Stars for the power play, the Avalanche at the penalty kill.

check.measure: expected goals per 60 on the power play
check.rule: held if tonight's figure lands on the predicted side of the league average; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: Strength against strength
claims.body: The Stars are one of the league’s best for chance quality, and the Avalanche are one of the league’s best at preventing dangerous shots. We’ll side with the Avalanche’s defense.
claims.call: The Avalanche keep the Stars’ chances less dangerous than the league average (a 6.3% chance of scoring on the average shot).
claims.nums: Dallas 4th for chance quality (a 6.7% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Colorado 2nd for preventing dangerous shots
claims.gist: It’s strength against strength: the Stars for chance quality, the Avalanche at preventing dangerous shots.

claims.head: The Stars get in close; the Avalanche shoot from distance
claims.body: The Stars are one of the league’s best for shots from in close, at the close-range end; the Avalanche are one of the league’s worst, at the long-range end. Expect that gap to show.
claims.nums: Shots from in close: Dallas 2nd, Colorado 31st
claims.gist: The Stars and the Avalanche sit at opposite ends for shots from in close.
claims.call: The Stars take a bigger share of their shots from within 20 feet than the Avalanche.

story.head: MacKinnon’s favourite opponent
paras: The Stars have won two in a row, the last a 4-0 rout of Buffalo. The Avalanche are 3-1-0.

items.text: Joel Kiviranta faces Colorado for the first time since leaving.
Nathan MacKinnon has a point in ten straight games against Dallas, and 18 points in his last eleven against them.
M. Duchene is out long term (lower body injury) and hasn’t played yet this season.
Wyatt Johnston is still looking for his first goal of the season.
